note: What an endpoint-keyed mark may claim, and what has to be true of what it captured. A mark is `rb:<kind> <selector>[,<selector>...] [<key>=<value>...]`, closed by `rb:end` where the block rule would stop short of what the author meant. A selector is family.endpoint for one, family.* for all of a family, or * for the target. harness/snippets.py reads this file and never learns a kind's name, so adding one is an object under `kinds` and a display section. The assertions are counted against the allowance rather than gated red: they fail on most of the corpus today and a red gate would block every branch that is fixing them. An allowance only ever goes down. --ratchet rewrites it from what the tree does, --check fails on anything above it.

handler.what: the lines that answer the request

wiring.what: the code that makes a feature family work, which the route does not name

not_only_annotations.label: annotation-only
not_only_annotations.what: a snippet may not be nothing but annotations, attributes and comments
not_only_annotations.why: @Get("/json/small") names the route, passes both coverage checks, and says nothing about what answers the request

reaches_domain.label: not reaching the domain
reaches_domain.what: a handler and its support together must name something the shared domain gave the file
reaches_domain.why: a registration that names a handler defined elsewhere is complete, correct, and shows a reader nothing. The shared domain is where the behaviour is, so a snippet that never gets there has not captured the endpoint. The exceptions are the two families that have no domain to reach: baseline.plaintext returns a literal, and the query family is parsing and coercion isolated from any use of the values

mentions_dep.label: wiring that does not name its dependency
mentions_dep.what: the support parts for a family must mention the dependency spec/matrix.json declares for it
mentions_dep.why: a mark that drifted onto neighbouring lines stops mentioning it, and a present mark is otherwise indistinguishable from a correct one
